messages:
alex_sales: Quick sync — Acme Health is asking whether our on-prem air-gapped POC can support offline cert rotation, delta upgrades, and license activation without egress. They also asked about bundle size and upgrade cadence. Anyone who owned the last POC can chime in?

maria.g: I ran a similar POC last quarter. We ship a signed offline bundle (tar.gz) + signature file. Ops can rsync/scp the bundle into their bastion and run the installer. We also support exporting OCI images to a tar and loading via `ctr images import`.

tim_ops: Confirmed. Cert rotation is the usual pain point. For isolated installs we accept a `ca_bundle.pem` at bootstrap and provide a rotation workflow that operates entirely offline. Example CLI for install: 
``nredwoodctl install --bundle redwood-1.14.0.tgz --ca ca_bundle.pem --license license.key
```
Note: that code block is run on the bastion that has access to the private cluster.

olivia_se: Do we have guidance on upgrade cadence for customers who want minimal maintenance windows? Acme asked about quarterly security-only patches vs full feature upgrades.

maria.g: Our recommendation: monthly security/minor patches (small deltas), feature releases quarterly. For Private we produce delta update bundles for patch releases (50–200MB typical) and full bundles for major upgrades. That keeps airgap transfers small.

alex_sales: How does offline license activation work? Customer legal wants to avoid any external callbacks.

tim_ops: We support offline activation. Customer generates a `license.activation.request` payload (JSON) from their install and sends it to us via a secure channel. We sign and return `license.key`. No callback required unless they opt-in for telemetry/license revalidation. If they choose no egress, we set longer TTL on the license and document revalidation procedures.

olivia_se: They also requested HSM/PKCS#11 and FIPS compatibility notes.

maria.g: HSM via PKCS#11 is supported in Private deployments; needs additional config during install (mount the token and provide slot info). FIPS builds are available on request but add ~2–3 weeks for QA and packaging. Call that out as an enterprise blocker in the SOW.

alex_sales: Pricing Q: POC vs production upgrades — will delta patches be billable? Customer is worried about hidden costs for monthly patches.

olivia_se: POC (30d) has no charges. Production will be on the reserved capacity or enterprise license. Delta patch delivery and support included in the support term (12-month). Extended maintenance/accelerated response is an add-on. I'll loop finance if they need exact numbers.

deploy-bot: release 1.14.0-rc2 artifacts pushed: s3://artifacts/redwood/1.14.0-rc2/ (signed).sha256 = abc123def456... :package:

tim_ops: For air-gapped customers we ship `redwood-1.14.0.tgz`, `redwood-1.14.0.tgz.sig`, and `sha256sum.txt`. Install checklist should include verifying the signature and sha256 before proceeding.

alex_sales: Good — I'll add that to the POC checklist. Anything else we should surface as potential blockers?

maria.g: Add these items to checklist: firewall rules (allow port 8443 between control plane and nodes inside cluster), time sync requirement (NTP), and disk space (bundle unpack + images ~ 12–20GB during install).

olivia_se: Add smoke tests we run post-install: `curl -k https://<host>:8443/healthz` to check readiness, and `redwoodctl token create --subject poc-test` to validate token issuance.

alex_sales: Also good to mention legal/EULA — they asked about redistribution. I'll cc @legal in the customer email.

maria.g: One more: if they require no external egress for license renewal, we can support multi-year license keys and documented offline renewal steps, but this is considered a contractual requirement.

alex_sales: Thanks everyone — I'll update the internal POC doc (https://redwood.internal/poc/acme-health) with the bundle flow, sample commands, and the checklist. Will drop a short playbook for the SE team. :thumbsup:
